To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the knee of the energy spectrum is located at 4.0+/-0.5 PeV, 2) at primary energies above 5-10 peV the primary particles exhibit a significant anisotropy, 3) the knee is a real feature of the primary spectrum, and 4) the knee is caused by a change in the composition of primary particles.
the knee region is anisotropic and the fraction of anisotropy in the knee region is about 10% (or 10 times less than in the region of primary cosmic rays with energies less than 10 PeV).

we have obtained the distribution of equatorial coordinates for EAS core directions in the knee region and that anisotropy of the primary cosmic rays is shown by declination equator coordinates only at primary energies more that ~5-10 Pev.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a search of a possible explanation for the observed anisotropy of cosmic rays at the knee.
the analysis of EAS parameters and anisotropy of EAS core coordinates in the knee region based on the data obtained at the MAKET-ANI station.
anisotropy analysis in the knee region based on EAS data obtained with MAKET-ANI array.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the knee region of primary spectrum is not the region of a sharp change of the primary cosmic rays spectrum but a transition region between two regions with different spectra.

the knee region is characterized by the following features: 1. the knee region is not a sharp energy threshold but a wide region of gradual energy change; 2. the knee region contains an anisotropic component with the fraction of ~10%; 3. the anisotropic component has the same energy spectrum as the isotropic component.
the observed EAS anisotropy in the knee region has a complex structure and is caused by the anisotropy of the galactic and extragalactic cosmic rays.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cosmic ray flux is not isotropic in the energy range of the knee.
we have found a clear anisotropic component of cosmic rays at primary energies more that 5-10PeV.
the anisotropy of cosmic rays is observed in the knee region and it is connected with the anisotropically of the sources.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the anisotropy of cosmic rays in the energy range of 1-10 PeV is not due to a change in the spectrum of cosmic rays, and is not associated with the knee phenomenon, but is due to the presence of a separate component in the spectrum of primary particles with an energy above the knee.
the anisotropy in the knee region is a feature of primary cosmic rays.
the knee region is a very promising area for searching for anisotropy of the primary CRs.
